newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SHORT-COVERINGS SLOW BUDAPEST GRAINS PRICES DROP.
newsitem.headline: SHORT-COVERINGS SLOW BUDAPEST GRAINS PRICES DROP.

text.p: Grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued their downward movement led by milling wheat on Thursday and there was no sign of a strong recovery, traders said.
"Milling wheat prices were supported to some extent by short-covering, but the (medium-term) downward trend will remain," said Dezso Kormendi of Swap brokerage.
Milling wheat prices dropped by 30 to 200 forints per tonne for al maturities except May which was flat at 24,810.

Milling wheat prices dropped by 1,500 to 1,700 forints since last Thursday pushed down by lower Chicago prices and expectations of a five million tonnes wheat crop this year, compared with 3.9 million tonnes in 1996.
Maize prices eased by 110 to 200 forints for three maturities, were flat for other three and went limit-up for July but Kormendi added that this sudden jump did not point to a trend.
"The settlement price (of July) was change by a last-minute deal of only 50 lots," he said.
An inverse spread was seen between October closing at 19,510 and November at 19,500 forints but Kormendi said market movement was likely to iron out this small crease shortly.
He added that maize futures trade was likely to concentrate on maturing July for the next few days.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was 1,141 lots or 488.49 million forints, slightly below Wednesday's 1,212 lots or 534.43 million forints.
